function.name: accept_changes
function.description: Accept pending tracked changes: insertions become plain text, deleted text disappears, new formatting stays. Select with all: true, ids from read_revisions, or any combination of author / type / blockIndex / blockRange / before. Only when the user asks to accept changes.

ids.description: revision ids from read_revisions (r1, r2, …); positional, so re-read after any edit

before.description: ISO date; only changes recorded before it

function.name: add_comment
function.description: Start a new comment thread on a block or on an exact text span inside it, without changing the document: review notes, questions, suggestions the user should decide on.

text.description: exact text inside the block to anchor the comment to; omitted = the whole block

occurrence.description: which match to anchor when text occurs more than once (1 = first)

comment.description: comment body; \n starts a new paragraph

author.description: author name; default: the AI author

initials.description: author initials shown in the margin

function.name: analyze_media
function.description: Look at a picture that is in the document and answer questions about it, or analyze image/audio/video given by URL or local file path; returns the analysis as text. An image block in the document carries no text of its own — read_blocks cannot tell you what a picture shows, so this is the only way to see it. Pass blockIndex for an image block listed by get_document_context, and/or mediaUrls.

blockIndex.description: block index of an image block of the document, as listed by get_document_context

mediaUrls.description: media URLs or local file paths (image/audio/video); optional when blockIndex is given

requirements.description: analysis requirements (English): what to extract, or the question to answer about the media

function.name: apply_ops
function.description: Run a list of formatting/structure ops as one atomic transaction (see the apply_ops guide in the system prompt): [generated at runtime]. Each op is a flat { op, target?, ...fields } object; fields are patches (present = set, null = clear, absent = untouched). Any invalid op rejects the whole batch with its usage line.

dryRun.description: validate and return the plan without changing the document

function.name: ask_clarification
function.description: Ask the user before an edit or an answer when the request is ambiguous about meaning, scope or target (which section or paragraphs, what a term or label in the document means, how far a rewrite should go). Shows a questionnaire card: 1–4 questions, ≤5 options each; the card adds "decide for me" and a free-text option itself. Use it only when a guess would likely change the wrong thing; skip it when the request or the document already answers it. Wait for the answers, then continue. Do not repeat the questions in your reply.

function.name: create_document
function.description: Create a NEW standalone file in the default save folder and open it in a new tab; the current document is not modified. Use when the user asks to put content into a new/separate document instead of this one. type 'docx' (default) and 'pdf' take the same restricted HTML as insert_content in content; type 'md' takes Markdown source; type 'html' takes a complete standalone HTML page (opens in the HTML editor). Images and charts are not supported in the new file's initial content.

title.description: document title, used as the file name

content.description: full document content: restricted HTML for docx/pdf, Markdown for md, a complete HTML page for html

function.name: define_style
function.description: Create a style or change the definition of an existing one (paragraph, character or table style in styles.xml). Only the fields given change; everything else the style already defines is kept. Paragraphs using the style pick the change up automatically. To put a style on paragraphs, call apply_ops with the applyStyle op { op: "applyStyle", target, styleId }. Existing style ids are listed by list_styles / in the tool output.

name.description: display name (defaults to the id when creating)

type.description: when creating (default paragraph); an existing style keeps its type

basedOn.description: parent style id to inherit from; null removes the inheritance

next.description: style of the paragraph created by Enter at the end of a paragraph in this style

quickFormat.description: show in the quick style gallery

spaceBefore.description: space before, a length like "0.5in", "1.27cm", "12pt" (bare numbers are points), or null to clear

spaceAfter.description: space after, a length like "0.5in", "1.27cm", "12pt" (bare numbers are points), or null to clear

lineSpacing.description: line spacing as a multiple of single (1, 1.15, 1.5, 2)

indentLeft.description: a length like "0.5in", "1.27cm", "12pt" (bare numbers are points), or null to clear

indentRight.description: a length like "0.5in", "1.27cm", "12pt" (bare numbers are points), or null to clear

firstLineIndent.description: first-line indent, negative = hanging indent, a length like "0.5in", "1.27cm", "12pt" (bare numbers are points), or null to clear

outlineLevel.description: 1-9: the style becomes a heading of that level in the navigation pane / TOC

highlight.description: highlight color name (yellow, green, cyan, magenta, blue, red, ...) or null

function.name: delete_comment
function.description: Delete a comment. A thread root with replies is refused unless withReplies is true; a reply id deletes just that reply.

id.description: id of the comment to delete

withReplies.description: also delete the replies of a thread root (default false)

function.name: delete_note
function.description: Remove a footnote or endnote together with its reference mark; ids from read_notes.

function.name: edit_chart
function.description: Edit the data of an existing chart in the document (title/category labels/series names/values). Chart blocks in the block list can be edited; the category count and the number of values per series must match the original chart (data points cannot be added or removed).

categories.description: new category labels, same length as the original; pass null for positions to keep

values.description: new values, same length as the original series; pass null for positions to keep

function.name: edit_note
function.description: Change the text of an existing footnote or endnote in place (findReplace inside the note): the note keeps its id, reference mark and formatting. Use for a typo or a citation fix instead of delete_note + insert_footnote.

kind.description: omit when the id is unambiguous across footnotes and endnotes

find.description: exact text inside the note to replace

function.name: generate_image
function.description: Generate an illustration with AI from a text prompt and insert it into the document (at the cursor / end of document). For illustration/diagram-style art that image_search cannot find, or when the user asks to generate/draw a picture.

prompt.description: detailed English description of the image to generate

function.name: get_document_context
function.description: Get the latest state of the current document: block list (index|type|content preview), full-text stats (word/character counts) and the current selection. Block indexes change after modifications; call this when you need up-to-date indexes.

function.name: image_search
function.description: Search for images. Returns a list of image imageUrl entries; after picking one, insert it into the document with insert_image.

function.name: insert_chart
function.description: Insert a chart (saved as a native Word chart). Data must be real: from the document content or web_search results — do not make up numbers.

series.description: data series; values has the same length as categories, use null for missing data. Pie charts use only the first series

afterBlockIndex.description: insert after this block index; -1 = start of document; omitted = after the block containing the cursor

function.name: insert_content
function.description: Insert new content at a given position (restricted HTML, may contain multiple blocks). For writing/continuing/generating new content; to rewrite existing content use replace_blocks.

afterBlockIndex.description: insert after this block index; -1 = start of document; omitted = after the block containing the cursor

function.name: insert_endnote
function.description: Add an endnote (same as insert_footnote, but the text collects at the end of the document). Use when the document already uses endnotes or the user asks for them.

blockIndex.description: block that gets the reference mark

afterText.description: exact text in that block the mark follows; omitted = end of the block

function.name: insert_footnote
function.description: Add a footnote: a superscript reference mark goes into the block (right after afterText, else at its end) and the note text prints at the bottom of that page. Use for sources, asides and clarifications the user asks to footnote.

blockIndex.description: block that gets the reference mark

afterText.description: exact text in that block the mark follows; omitted = end of the block

function.name: insert_image
function.description: Download a direct image link (an imageUrl from image_search) and insert it into the document (at the cursor / end of document).

function.name: insert_picture
function.description: Insert a picture from a direct image link at a block position, at a given size, inline or floating (positioned on the page, with text wrapping around/behind/in front). insert_image is the simpler cursor-position variant.

afterBlockIndex.description: insert after this block (-1 = start of document); default: end of document

width.description: display width, "2.54cm", "1in", "72pt", "96px" or a bare number of points; default natural size capped at 480px

height.description: display height; omit to keep the aspect ratio

float.description: omit for an inline picture in its own paragraph; give it to float the picture at a position

anchor.description: what x/y measure from: the anchor paragraph (x from the text column, y from the paragraph top), the page corner, or the margin box corner

x.description: horizontal offset, "2.54cm", "1in", "72pt", "96px" or a bare number of points

y.description: vertical offset, "2.54cm", "1in", "72pt", "96px" or a bare number of points

wrap.description: how body text flows around it (default square)

function.name: insert_section_break
function.description: Insert a section break after a block so the blocks after it form a new section with its own page setup, headers and footers (the new section starts as a copy of the current one; change it with set_page_setup afterwards). type nextPage starts the new section on a new page, continuous keeps the flow (needed for column changes mid-page), evenPage / oddPage start on the next even / odd page.

afterBlockIndex.description: the break goes after this block index; -1 = before the first block

function.name: insert_text_box
function.description: Insert a floating text box (a positioned rectangle holding text, like a callout or sidebar) anchored to a block. Body text either flows above/below it or ignores it.

afterBlockIndex.description: anchor after this block (-1 = start of document); default: end of document

width.description: box width, "2.54cm", "1in", "72pt", "96px" or a bare number of points

height.description: box height, "2.54cm", "1in", "72pt", "96px" or a bare number of points

x.description: horizontal offset, "2.54cm", "1in", "72pt", "96px" or a bare number of points

y.description: vertical offset, "2.54cm", "1in", "72pt", "96px" or a bare number of points

anchor.description: offsets measure from the anchor paragraph (default) or the page corner

wrap.description: body text resumes below the box (default for paragraph anchors) or ignores it (default for page anchors)

fontSize.description: text size in points (a bare number, or a length like "12pt")

function.name: list_styles
function.description: List the styles defined in the document (id, name, type, parent, heading level) for define_style / applyStyle.

function.name: read_attachment
function.description: Read the text content of an attachment (parsed locally). Long files are paged: read offset=0 first, then decide whether to continue based on the returned total character count.

index.description: attachment index (0-based, see the attachment list)

function.name: read_blocks
function.description: Read the full content of a block range (restricted HTML). Previews in the block list are truncated; you must read the full original text with this tool before rewriting. Long ranges are paged: a truncated result says which offset to continue from; concatenate the slices in order to get the full HTML.

offset.description: character offset to continue a truncated read (default 0); use the offset given in the previous truncation notice

function.name: read_comments
function.description: List all comment threads (including resolved ones) with ids, authors, anchored block indexes and anchor text. Unresolved threads already ride along in the message context; use this for the full picture.

function.name: read_notes
function.description: List every footnote and endnote with its id, number, the block holding its reference mark and its text.

function.name: read_revisions
function.description: List every pending tracked revision (insertions, deletions, formatting/move/table changes) with its id, type, author, date, block index, the affected text and, for formatting changes, what changed. Ids are positional (r1 = first in document order) and renumber after every edit, so read again before accept_changes / reject_changes.

function.name: reject_changes
function.description: Reject pending tracked changes: inserted text disappears, deleted text is restored, formatting goes back to what it was. Same selector as accept_changes. Only when the user asks to reject changes.

ids.description: revision ids from read_revisions (r1, r2, …); positional, so re-read after any edit

before.description: ISO date; only changes recorded before it

function.name: replace_blocks
function.description: Replace a block range with new content (restricted HTML). For rewriting/translating/condensing/expanding existing content; the new block count may differ from the old. New blocks inherit the replaced blocks' paragraph and text formatting (font, size, color, indent, spacing, alignment) automatically, and a rewritten <table> keeps the old table's column widths, borders, shading and cell formatting (unchanged cells keep their content); never try to restore formatting afterwards.

function.name: replace_selection
function.description: Replace exactly the user's selected text (the <sel>…</sel> span in the context) with new inline content, leaving the rest of the block untouched. For rewording/translating/correcting a selected phrase or sentence inside a paragraph. The new text inherits the selection's formatting unless the fragment styles it. Requires a range selection inside one paragraph/heading/list item; for whole blocks or several blocks use replace_blocks.

html.description: replacement inline content: plain text or restricted inline HTML (strong em u s a br formula)

function.name: reply_comment
function.description: Add a reply to a comment thread: after completing a requested change (summarize what changed), or to answer/ask back when the comment is a question or is ambiguous.

parentId.description: id of the comment thread to reply to

function.name: resolve_comment
function.description: Mark a comment thread as resolved. Only after the requested change was applied (reply first), or when the user explicitly asked to resolve.

id.description: id of the comment thread to resolve

function.name: set_header_footer
function.description: Set the page header or footer text (the current contents are listed in the message context). Plain text; \n separates lines; the tokens {PAGE} and {NUMPAGES} become live page-number fields; an empty string clears the text. Per-line alignment/styling of the existing header/footer is preserved; images in it are untouched. view "first"/"even" writes the different-first-page / even-page variant (enabling that setting if needed).

text.description: new text; \n between lines; may contain {PAGE} / {NUMPAGES}; "" clears

view.description: which variant to write (default when omitted)

function.name: set_page_setup
function.description: Change paper size, orientation, margins, text columns, the different-first-page flag or page numbering of the document or of one section (the message context lists the sections). Only the fields given change. Lengths take a unit suffix (cm, mm, in, pt) or twips. Setting the orientation alone swaps the current width and height.

section.description: section index (0-based) to change; omit with blockIndex omitted = every section

blockIndex.description: change the section that contains this block index

paper.description: named size: A3, A4, A5, B5, Letter, Legal, Tabloid

width.description: custom page width, a number of twips or a string with a unit: "2.54cm", "1in", "72pt", "10mm"

height.description: custom page height, a number of twips or a string with a unit: "2.54cm", "1in", "72pt", "10mm"

margins.description: any of top, right, bottom, left, header, footer, gutter; each a number of twips or a string with a unit: "2.54cm", "1in", "72pt", "10mm"

header.description: header distance from the page top

footer.description: footer distance from the page bottom

spacing.description: gap between columns, a number of twips or a string with a unit: "2.54cm", "1in", "72pt", "10mm"

titlePg.description: different first page (own header/footer on the first page of the section)

pageNumberStart.description: restart page numbering at this value; null = continue from the previous section

function.name: set_watermark
function.description: Set, restyle or remove the page watermark: a gray text like DRAFT or CONFIDENTIAL, or a washed-out picture (a logo), drawn behind the body on every page (written into the page header, where Word shows it in Design > Watermark). Give text or image, not both; text null or image null removes whichever watermark the document has.

text.description: watermark text; null removes the watermark

fontFamily.description: font face (default the document theme face)

image.description: picture watermark: http(s) or data: URL of a png/jpg/gif, centered behind the body; null removes the watermark

scale.description: picture size as a percent of its natural size (default: fit the page inside the margins)

washout.description: fade the picture like Word's washout (default true)

function.name: web_search
function.description: Search the web for textual information (references/data/facts). Use when you need up-to-date information or are unsure about a fact. Returns titles/links/snippets.

function.name: write_document
function.description: [For long new content: a whole document, a chapter, a full report, article or translation] Hands the writing to the system writer, which streams restricted HTML straight into the document while the user watches; you never write the text yourself. Give a concrete plan (title, section outline with the key points of each, tone, target length) and put every fact, figure, name and quote the text must use into context — the writer sees only the plan and context, not the conversation. Omit afterBlockIndex on a blank document; on a document with content, pass afterBlockIndex to insert after that block, or replaceDocument=true when the user asked to rewrite everything. Short additions (a paragraph or two) use insert_content instead.

plan.description: title, section outline with key points per section, tone, target length

title.description: document/chapter title, when there is one

context.description: reference material: facts, figures, quotes, sources gathered from the conversation, attachments and web_search

afterBlockIndex.description: insert after this block index (-1 = document start); omitted = whole document

replaceDocument.description: true replaces all existing content (only when the user asked for a rewrite)

function.name: aggregate_range
function.description: Compute statistics for a range without reading or modifying it cell by cell: non-empty count, distinct-value count, numeric sum/average/min/max, and the most frequent values. Handles very large ranges (up to 1,000,000 cells) efficiently. ALWAYS use this for questions like "how many distinct suppliers/customers", value distributions, or column totals on large sheets — never loop read_range over big data and never write COUNTIF/SUMPRODUCT distinct-count formulas (they are rejected as too expensive). Aggregate one column at a time for meaningful distinct counts.

range.description: Range like "D2:D88588" (typically one column, excluding the header)

sheetId.description: Target sheet id; the active sheet when omitted

topValues.description: How many most-frequent values to return (0-50, default 10)

skipHiddenRows.description: Leave out hidden/filtered rows (visible rows only, like SUBTOTAL). Default false: they are included, like SUM. The result always states how many there were and whether they were included — repeat that in your answer.

function.name: ask_clarification
function.description: [Before calculating or writing when the meaning or the target is unclear] Show a question card so the user confirms what you would otherwise guess: what a column holds (e.g. whether column X, Y or Z is net revenue, or whether "Amount" includes tax), which rows count, or which range the result goes into. Ask only what the data and the request do not answer (read the headers and a sample first); 1–4 questions, ≤5 options each, built from what you actually see (header names, ranges); the card adds "decide for me" and a free-text option itself. Skip it when the request is already clear. Wait for the answers, then continue with them. Do not repeat the questions in your reply.

function.name: compare_ranges
function.description: Read-only reconciliation of two ranges (two sheets, or a ledger vs a bank export), computed by code: rows are matched on a key column (trimmed, case-insensitive), and the result lists keys found only on the left, only on the right, and matched keys whose compared values differ (with right − left for numbers). Compared columns pair by identical header text unless leftColumns/rightColumns give explicit pairs. A number and the same digits stored as text count as different, never cast. Coverage is always reported: rows processed per side, blank and duplicate keys, hidden rows, and total/subtotal rows (left out by default). Use it instead of reading both ranges and comparing them yourself.

leftRange.description: First table, e.g. "A1:F500" (header in the first row unless hasHeader=false)

leftSheetId.description: Sheet of leftRange (id from get_workbook_context); the active sheet when omitted

leftKey.description: Key column letter in leftRange, e.g. "A"

leftColumns.description: Column letters to compare on the left, paired by position with rightColumns

rightSheetId.description: Sheet of rightRange; the active sheet when omitted

rightColumns.description: Column letters to compare on the right, same count as leftColumns

hasHeader.description: Both ranges start with a header row (default true)

tolerance.description: Numbers whose absolute difference is at most this compare equal (default 0)

skipHiddenRows.description: Leave out hidden/filtered rows on both sides (default false: included and counted)

includeTotalRows.description: Also match rows detected as totals/subtotals (default false: left out and listed)

maxListed.description: How many missing keys and differences to list per section (1-200, default 50)

function.name: create_document
function.description:
Create a NEW standalone file in the default save folder and open it in a new tab; the current workbook is not modified. Types 'xlsx' (default) and 'csv' export ONE worksheet of THIS workbook: pass sheetId (defaults to the active sheet); the file gets the sheet's current displayed values (formula results; formulas and formatting are not carried over) and content must be omitted. To split a workbook into separate files, call once per sheet. To export data that is not in a sheet yet, write it into a new sheet first (add_sheet + set_range), then export that sheet. Types 'docx' and 'pdf' take simple HTML in content (

-

    /
      /
    1. , , 
      , 
      ; inline ///); type 'md' takes Markdown source; type 'html' takes a complete standalone HTML page (opens in the HTML editor) — use these when the user wants a report/summary as its own document. title becomes the file name; xlsx/csv default it to the worksheet name.

sheetId.description: xlsx/csv only: the worksheet to export (id from get_workbook_context); defaults to the active sheet

title.description: file name without extension (required for docx/pdf/md; xlsx/csv default to the sheet name)

content.description: docx/pdf: simple HTML; md: Markdown source. Forbidden for xlsx/csv — their data comes from the worksheet

function.name: find_cells
function.description: Search the whole workbook (or one sheet) for cells whose value or formula matches a query; returns Sheet!Address with the cell content. Plain text matches as a case-insensitive substring; regex=true treats the query as a case-insensitive JavaScript regex; errors_only=true finds formula error cells (#REF!, #DIV/0!, #VALUE!, #NAME?, #N/A, #NUM!, #NULL!) and query may then be omitted. For formula cells the matched value is the last calculated value. Prefer this over paging read_range when locating data or auditing errors.

query.description: Text or regex to find; may be omitted only when errors_only=true

regex.description: Treat query as a JavaScript regex (default false)

sheetId.description: Restrict the search to one sheet; searches every sheet when omitted

errors_only.description: Find cells whose calculated value is a formula error (default false)

function.name: generate_image
function.description: Generate an image with AI from a text prompt. Returns a URL to insert with propose_operations add_image. Use for illustrations/decorative art; prefer image_search for real-world subjects.

prompt.description: What to draw — subject, style, composition (English works better)

function.name: get_workbook_context
function.description: Get a workbook overview: all sheets (id/name/data-extent rows-columns), active sheet, current selection, known non-empty cell addresses. For data-size questions (how many rows / how much data), answer from the data extent here instead of reading block by block; use read_range or read_cells when concrete values are needed.

function.name: image_search
function.description: Search the web for images. Returns a numbered list of direct imageUrl entries with pixel sizes; pick one and insert it with propose_operations add_image (path = the URL).

function.name: load_guide
function.description: Load operation guide documents into context (field definitions, conventions, common mistakes). Except for the most basic single-cell reads/writes, load the relevant guides before generating propose_operations; several can be loaded at once. Available guides: [generated at runtime]

function.name: merge_attached_workbooks
function.description: Import every sheet of the attached spreadsheet files (xlsx/xlsm/xls/csv) into the current workbook, engine-side. Returns the created sheet names. Use this before analyzing or restructuring attached spreadsheet data; never rebuild attachment contents cell-by-cell from text.

indexes.description: Attachment indexes to merge (0-based, from the attachment list). Omit to merge every spreadsheet attachment.

function.name: propose_operations
function.description: Submit a batch of change operations, applied to the workbook immediately (the user can roll back with the [Undo] button or ⌘Z). Basic operations: {op:"set_cell",sheetId,address,value} | {op:"set_formula",sheetId,address,formula(starts with =)} | {op:"clear_cell",sheetId,address} | {op:"rename_sheet",sheetId,name}. Field definitions for the remaining operations live in the guides — load_guide before using them: writing(set_range/fill_range/copy_range/convert_to_values/clear_range/find_replace) | formatting(format_range) | layout(sort_range/merge_cells/unmerge_cells/set_row_height/set_col_width/set_rows_hidden/set_cols_hidden/set_freeze/set_page_setup) | structure(insert_rows/delete_rows/insert_cols/delete_cols/add_sheet/delete_sheet/duplicate_sheet/set_sheet_hidden/move_sheet/protect_sheet) | charts(add_chart/edit_chart/delete_visual/add_sparkline/add_shape/edit_shape/add_image) | pivot(add_pivot/refresh_pivot) | table(add_table/add_table_row/add_table_column/delete_table_row/delete_table_column/delete_table) | data(set_hyperlink/set_filter/clear_filter/set_filter_criteria/add_conditional_format/clear_conditional_formats/set_data_validation/set_note/add_defined_name/delete_defined_name). Limits: structural operations (row/column insert-delete, sheet add/delete/duplicate/move/hide) cannot share a batch with other classes; at most 2000 expanded cell changes — except the range-level bulk ops fill_range / copy_range / convert_to_values / clear_range / find_replace / sort_range / format_range, which handle up to 200,000 cells in one op (use fill_range to fill a formula or pattern down a whole column instead of huge set_range batches, copy_range to duplicate a large block once, convert_to_values to freeze formulas into their computed values); sheetId must be an id returned by get_workbook_context.

operations.description: Array of operations in the workbook DSL discriminated-union format

summary.description: One-sentence summary of this batch of changes

function.name: read_attachment
function.description: Read an attachment's text content (parsed locally). Long files are paged: read offset=0 first, then decide whether to continue based on the returned total character count.

index.description: Attachment index (0-based, see the attachment list)

function.name: read_cells
function.description: Read current values/formulas of specific scattered cells (use read_range for contiguous regions). Always read the affected cells before writing — never assume their contents. A cell whose stored value differs from its shown text carries a [type; raw value; number format] note, e.g. "A1: 10% [percent; raw 0.1; format 0%]" vs "A2: 10" (a plain number) vs "A3: 10 [text]" — calculate with the raw value; unannotated cells are plain text or General-format numbers.

addresses.description: List of cell addresses, e.g. ["A1","B2"], max 100

sheetId.description: Sheet to read from (id from get_workbook_context); reads the active sheet when omitted

function.name: read_formats
function.description: Read explicit cell formats in a range (bold/italic/underline/colors/number format/alignment/borders); only formatted cells are returned. Use when you need to "reuse the format from somewhere" or inspect current formatting; max 200 cells.

sheetId.description: Sheet to read from (id from get_workbook_context); reads the active sheet when omitted

function.name: read_range
function.description: Read current values/formulas by rectangular range, returning a grid with row numbers and column letters. The requested range is not the worksheet data extent: never infer total row or record count from its ending row; use get_workbook_context. This is the preferred way to read data; max 2000 cells — read larger regions in multiple calls. The grid shows the text as displayed; cells whose stored value differs (percent, currency, date, numbers with a format, numeric-looking text) are listed under it as [type; raw value; number format], e.g. "B2: percent; raw 0.1; format 0%" — calculate with the raw value (dates are serial numbers). Hidden/filtered rows are labelled in the grid.

range.description: Range like "A1:D20"; a single cell like "B2" is also accepted

sheetId.description: Sheet to read from (id from get_workbook_context); reads the active sheet when omitted

function.name: read_sheet_features
function.description: Read a worksheet's feature state: AutoFilter (range and column criteria), conditional formatting rules, data validation rules, defined names, freeze panes, hidden/protected status, shapes and images, and page setup pending save this session. Read the current state before modifying or clearing any of these existing settings — never change them blindly.

sheetId.description: Target sheet id; reads the active sheet when omitted

function.name: select_range
function.description: Select a range in the grid and scroll the user's view to it, activating its sheet. Pure view navigation — changes no data, but it does replace whatever the user had selected. function.name: summarize_range
function.description: Read-only conditional statistics over a table range, computed by code: sum / count / average / min / max of one column, optionally filtered by conditions on other columns (all must hold, like SUMIFS/COUNTIFS) and grouped by a column (like a pivot). Use it for "total revenue for Hà Nội", "count of orders per region", "average price where qty > 10" — instead of writing COUNTIFS/SUMIFS helper cells or adding numbers yourself. Columns are Excel column letters of the sheet (read the header row first to map names like X/Y/Z to letters). Only real numbers are summed: text such as "1.234,5", blanks, booleans and errors are skipped and counted by reason, never converted. Text conditions match case-insensitively; >, >=, <, <= compare numbers only (dates are serial numbers). The result reports the range, the filter, rows processed/matching, hidden/filtered rows and every skipped cell — state these in your answer. Up to 1,000,000 cells.

function.name: apply_ops
function.description:
[Canonical edit surface] Apply a list of canonical edit ops as ONE transaction — atomic by default: any failure rolls everything back, nothing is half-applied. Set dry_run:true to validate the plan without touching the deck (rehearse risky batches). This is THE tool for every edit without a dedicated tool (fill, stroke, transform, delete, z-order, grouping, crop, opacity, effects, links, table cells, structure and styling, page background, speaker notes, page delete/move/duplicate, transitions, sections, theme) and for multi-page or many-element batches; a single op is a perfectly fine batch. For one-page layout math prefer execute_slide_script.
Addressing: every op takes target:{slide, el?} — slide = 0-based index or durable "s_<n>"; el = an element id from the outline/read_slide (e_* ids are durable). Group children: put the child id in target.el and add group:"<group id>".
Units are document-space EMU. read_slide reports px and its exact "1 px = N EMU" factor — convert with that N (9525 only on a standard 16:9 deck; other page sizes differ). Font sizes are pt.
Full op reference (the same executor every editing surface uses), one signature per op; ? marks optional fields:

function.name: execute_slide_script
function.description:
[Preferred tool for editing a slide's existing elements] Runs your JS edit script against one page; a single script covers: position/size/alignment/distribution/relative nudges/text/style/fill/stroke. At run time the script automatically receives the real geometry and text of every element on the page (els) — **no read_slide needed first**; read-write combined, compute from els inside the script. The whole script is one atomic transaction: geometry in one batch, the rest in script order, one undo step; if any operation fails, everything rolls back and the page is unchanged — fix the script and resend it whole. A layout audit (overlap/out-of-bounds/text overflow) is returned at the end. Far more reliable than individual set_element_* calls — coordinate math happens at execution site, not from memory. If the audit reports problems, call this tool again immediately to fix.
Script environment (constrained synchronous JS-like DSL; no external APIs or ambient globals):
- els: array, each item {id,type,text,x,y,w,h,rotation,fontSizePt?,fill?,textColor?,strokeColor?,inGroup?,groupId?,locked?} (pixels, origin top-left; fill/textColor/strokeColor are current colors in #RRGGBB, read-only — write via setFill/setStyle/setStroke; inGroup+groupId=directly editable group child (all primitives work, coordinates absolute as shown); inGroup without groupId=nested in a sub-group, read-only — apply_ops ungroupElement on the outer group first; locked=layout decoration, read-only)
- canvas: {w,h} canvas size (px)
- setBox(id, {x?,y?,w?,h?,rotation?}): set an element's target box, pass only fields to change
- moveBy(id, dx, dy): relative move (left = negative dx, up = negative dy)
- resizeBy(id, dw, dh): relative resize
- setText(id, textOrParagraphs): replace text entirely; pass a string (split into paragraphs by \n) or a paragraph array (same format as apply_ops setText paragraphs)
- setStyle(id, {fontSize?,color?,bold?,italic?,underline?,align?,fontFamily?}): change style without changing text, pass only fields to change
- setFill(id, colorOrNone): solid fill '#RRGGBB' or 'none'
- setStroke(id, {color?,widthPt?} | null): stroke; pass null to remove
- log(...): debug output (echoed back to you); the return value is echoed back to you (put a summary there)
- Supported computation: const/let, arithmetic, if/for/for...of/while, functions/arrows, JSON object/array literals, Math, regex.test, and safe array/string methods. No classes, async, modules, constructors, prototypes, or dynamic code.
Example 1 — three cards equal width, equal spacing:
const cards = els.filter(e => /card/.test(e.id));
const gap = 32, w = (canvas.w - 2*80 - (cards.length-1)*gap) / cards.length;
cards.forEach((c, i) => setBox(c.id, { x: 80 + i*(w+gap), y: 200, w, h: 320 }));
Example 2 — move the title left a bit: moveBy('title', -30, 0);
Example 3 — make the title blue and bold: setStyle('t1', { color: '#1a73e8', bold: true });

code.description: JS script body (synchronous code; may use els/canvas plus setBox/moveBy/resizeBy/setText/setStyle/setFill/setStroke/log; may return a summary)

explanation.description: One sentence describing what this script does (≤60 chars, shown to the user)

function.name: generate_deck
function.description: [First choice for creating a whole new deck — self-driven pipeline: auto image search, page-by-page generation with live display, no missing pages] Recommended usage (especially with many pages): pass only topic + approx_pages (+ optional style/context); the system plans the outline internally (auto-batched beyond 12 pages), **auto-searches images** (no advance image_search — the system searches from the planned image_queries keywords internally and fills real URLs back before writing HTML), writes HTML page by page, and lands pages onto the canvas one by one. You don't hand-write dozens of pages, and neither "only page 1 got generated" nor "arguments were truncated" can happen — the page count is guaranteed by the system loop. (If you already know each page you may pass core_hook+style+pages directly; pages[].image_queries takes English image-search keywords, searched internally; if you already know real http(s) URLs pass them directly — the system respects existing URLs and does not re-search.) To add a few pages to an existing deck, pass pages (briefs for just the new pages) + insert_mode:"append".

bold.description: Set the replacement in the bold variant

italic.description: Set the replacement in the italic variant

function.name: extract_pages
function.description: Copy the given pages into a new PDF. IRREVERSIBLE FILE OPERATION: the user is asked to confirm in a card first; on confirm every unsaved edit is saved to disk (cannot be undone) and the result is written as a NEW file in the default save folder and opened in a new tab; the current document keeps its pages.

pages.description: Original page numbers as a range string, e.g. "1-3,5"

function.name: flip_image
function.description: Mirror an existing page image horizontally (left-right as displayed) or vertically (top-bottom as displayed) in place; footprint and z-order kept (takes effect on save). Call list_page_images first; image_number refers to that listing.

image_number.description: Image number from list_page_images (1-based, per page)

axis.description: 'horizontal' mirrors left-right, 'vertical' mirrors top-bottom, both as the page is displayed

function.name: generate_image
function.description: Generate an image with AI from a text prompt; returns an image URL to pass to insert_image. Use for custom illustrations/icons/diagrams; for real photos prefer image_search.

prompt.description: Image description, English works better (keep any text to render in the image verbatim)

function.name: get_outline
function.description: Read the document outline (bookmarks) tree, including entry titles. Returns empty if the document has no outline.

function.name: goto_page
function.description: Scroll the reading view to the given page so the user can see it.

function.name: image_search
function.description: Search the web for images. Returns a numbered list with direct imageUrl links; pick one and pass its URL to insert_image. Use for real photos/logos; use generate_image for custom illustrations.

function.name: insert_blank_page
function.description: Insert a blank page (same size as its neighbor) after the given page; after_page 0 inserts it as the first page. IRREVERSIBLE FILE OPERATION: the user is asked to confirm in a card first; on confirm every unsaved edit is saved and the file on disk is rewritten, which cannot be undone. Afterwards the document reloads and page numbers change; re-read (search_text/read_pages) before any further edit. Prefer apply_ops (deletePage / setPageOrder / rotatePages) when it suffices.

after_page.description: Original page number to insert after (1-based); 0 = insert as the first page

function.name: insert_image
function.description: Download an image URL (from image_search or generate_image) and place it on a page (takes effect on save). Position it either with anchor_text (a verbatim text fragment on the page) plus placement, or with explicit x/y in points measured from the page top-left as displayed; with neither, the image is centered on the page.

url.description: Direct image link (from image_search or generate_image)

anchor_text.description: Verbatim text fragment on the page to position the image relative to

placement.description: Which side of anchor_text to place the image on; defaults to below

x.description: Left edge in points from the page left edge as displayed

y.description: Top edge in points from the page TOP edge as displayed

width.description: Display width in PDF points; height follows the aspect ratio. Default: natural size, capped to half the page width

layer.description: Z-order relative to the page text; below_text (default) never covers text

function.name: insert_text
function.description: Add NEW text to a page (drawn as new content on top of the page; takes effect on save). Use this for blank pages, empty areas, and filling in non-interactive form blanks — to change text that already exists, use edit_text or edit_block instead. Position with anchor_text (a verbatim fragment on the page, e.g. a form label) plus placement, or with x/y as the TOP-LEFT corner of the text block in points measured from the page top-left as displayed; with neither, the block is centered horizontally near the top. "\n" starts a new line; pass max_width to auto-wrap long paragraphs within that width.

anchor_text.description: Verbatim text fragment on the page (e.g. a form label) to position the new text against

placement.description: Which side of anchor_text to place the text on; defaults to right

x.description: Left edge of the text block in points from the page left edge

y.description: Top edge of the text block in points from the page TOP edge

font_size.description: Font size in PDF points; defaults to 14

color.description: Text color as #RRGGBB hex; defaults to black

max_width.description: Wrap width in points: paragraphs are re-wrapped to fit; omit to keep the given line breaks as-is

align.description: Line alignment within max_width (or the widest line); defaults to left

font.description: Font for the text; ignored when the face lacks glyphs for it (e.g. CJK). Omit for automatic

bold.description: Set the text in the bold variant

italic.description: Set the text in the italic variant

function.name: list_form_fields
function.description: List all form fields in the document (name/type/current value/options/page). Must be called before filling forms to learn the fields.

function.name: list_inserted_text
function.description: List the text blocks added with insert_text this session that are still unsaved: id, page, top-left position in points as displayed, font size, and a text preview. Their ids feed edit_inserted_text / move_inserted_text / delete_inserted_text. Once the user saves, inserted text becomes page content and is no longer listed — change it with edit_text then.

page.description: Only list blocks on this page (1-based); omit for all

function.name: list_page_images
function.description: List the images embedded in the page content: per-page image numbers with position/size in points as displayed (x from the left edge, y from the page TOP, page rotation applied). Call this before transform_image or delete_image. Images inserted in this session but not yet saved are not listed.

page.description: Page number (1-based); omit to list images on every page

function.name: markup_text
function.description: Add a markup (highlight/underline/strikeout) to a text passage on the given page. text must be a verbatim fragment that actually exists on that page (confirm with read_pages or search_text first); by default only the first occurrence is marked, all=true marks every occurrence on that page.

text.description: Verbatim text fragment from the page

all.description: Whether to mark every occurrence on the page; defaults to false

color.description: Markup color as #RRGGBB hex; omit to use the user's current color for the type

function.name: merge_pages
function.description: N-up imposition: place per_sheet consecutive pages onto one sheet (e.g. 2 = two pages side by side). IRREVERSIBLE FILE OPERATION: the user is asked to confirm in a card first; on confirm every unsaved edit is saved to disk (cannot be undone) and the result is written as a NEW file in the default save folder and opened in a new tab; the current document keeps its pages.

direction.description: Fill order: horizontal = left to right then down, vertical = top to bottom then right (default)

separator.description: Draw hairlines between the placed pages (default false)

function.name: move_inserted_text
function.description: Move an unsaved inserted text block (same as the user dragging it). Give x/y as the new TOP-LEFT corner in points from the page top-left as displayed, or dx/dy as an offset in points (positive dy moves down). Only pending inserts can be moved; saved text is page content.

x.description: New left edge in points from the page left edge

y.description: New top edge in points from the page top edge

function.name: move_text_block
function.description: Move a whole paragraph to another position on its page without changing its text (takes effect on save; fonts and spacing are kept as-is). The paragraph is located like in edit_block: paragraph_text must match exactly one paragraph. dx/dy are the offset in PDF points as displayed: positive dx moves right, positive dy moves DOWN on screen (negative dy moves up). Nothing else on the page moves, so check the target area is free (read the page layout first). Typical use: after deleting a paragraph, move the following paragraph up by the deleted height to close the gap.

paragraph_text.description: Verbatim fragment identifying the paragraph; must match exactly one paragraph on the page

dx.description: Horizontal offset in points; positive moves right

dy.description: Vertical offset in points as displayed; positive moves down, negative up

function.name: read_annotations
function.description: List the comment notes (sticky notes, with their reply threads) and text markups (highlight/underline/strikeout) in the document — both saved in the file and queued unsaved this session. Optional page range; omit to read the whole document. Reply to a note with reply_note or change its text with edit_note using the returned note ids (replies have their own ids).

start.description: First page (1-based); omit to start at page 1

end.description: Last page (inclusive); omit to read to the end

function.name: read_pages
function.description: Read the text content of a page range (with [Page N] markers). Read the relevant pages before answering questions; at most 10 pages per call, over-long output is truncated.

end.description: End page number (inclusive); if omitted, only the start page is read

function.name: remove_image_background
function.description: Remove the background of an existing page image (makes the edge-connected background color transparent, like "Remove Background" in Office); footprint and z-order kept (takes effect on save). Works best on photos/logos on a plain background. Call list_page_images first; image_number refers to that listing.

image_number.description: Image number from list_page_images (1-based, per page)

tolerance.description: Color tolerance 0-100 (default 30); raise it when background remains, lower it when parts of the subject disappear

function.name: replace_image
function.description: Swap an existing page image's pixels for a downloaded URL (from image_search or generate_image) in place — footprint and z-order survive; the new image stretches to the old footprint (takes effect on save). Call list_page_images first; image_number refers to that listing. This is the tool for "change/AI-edit this image": generate_image with the desired edit, then replace_image with the returned URL.

image_number.description: Image number from list_page_images (1-based, per page)

function.name: replace_pages
function.description: Replace the given pages with all pages of another PDF. A native file picker opens for the user to choose that PDF. IRREVERSIBLE FILE OPERATION: the user is asked to confirm in a card first; on confirm every unsaved edit is saved and the file on disk is rewritten, which cannot be undone. Afterwards the document reloads and page numbers change; re-read (search_text/read_pages) before any further edit. Prefer apply_ops (deletePage / setPageOrder / rotatePages) when it suffices.

pages.description: Original page numbers to replace as a range string, e.g. "1-3,5"

function.name: reply_note
function.description: Append a reply to an existing note thread (takes effect on save; authored as "AI Assistant"). note_id is a thread id from read_annotations.

page.description: Page number (1-based) the thread is on

function.name: rotate_image
function.description: Rotate an existing page image about its center (takes effect on save). Call list_page_images first; image_number refers to that listing. Quarter turns only; the footprint width/height swap for 90°/270°.

image_number.description: Image number from list_page_images (1-based, per page)

direction.description: cw = 90° clockwise (default), ccw = 90° counter-clockwise, 180 = half turn

function.name: search_text
function.description: Search the full text for a string; returns the page number and a context excerpt for each hit. Prefer this when locating which page something is on.

function.name: set_header_footer
function.description: Set the header and footer stamped on every page (takes effect on save): six text slots (header/footer × left/center/right) plus an automatic page number in the footer center. Text may contain {page} and {total} placeholders. The call replaces the header/footer set earlier this session — omitted slots become empty — and a call with every slot empty and page_number false removes it.

page_number.description: Print the page number in the footer center (overrides footer_center); default false

start_at.description: Number of the first page when page_number is on (default 1)

function.name: set_image_opacity
function.description: Make an existing page image semi-transparent (fade/watermark look) by baking the opacity into its pixels; footprint and z-order kept (takes effect on save). Absolute, not cumulative. Call list_page_images first; image_number refers to that listing.

image_number.description: Image number from list_page_images (1-based, per page)

opacity.description: Resulting opacity from 0 (invisible) to 1 (fully opaque); e.g. 0.5 = half transparent

function.name: set_page_size
function.description: Resize every page of the document to a paper size (content scaled to fit, portrait). Pass either preset or both width and height in points. IRREVERSIBLE FILE OPERATION: the user is asked to confirm in a card first; on confirm every unsaved edit is saved and the file on disk is rewritten, which cannot be undone. Afterwards the document reloads and page numbers change; re-read (search_text/read_pages) before any further edit. Prefer apply_ops (deletePage / setPageOrder / rotatePages) when it suffices.

width.description: Page width in points (when no preset)

height.description: Page height in points (when no preset)

function.name: set_watermark
function.description: Add or replace a text watermark drawn diagonally across every page (takes effect on save); pass text "" to remove the watermark added this session. It is stamped above the page content and cannot remove a watermark that is part of the original document.

size.description: Font size as a fraction of the page width, 0.02–0.5 (default 0.11)

function.name: split_pages
function.description: Cut every page into a grid of 2, 4, or 9 smaller pages (inverse of merge_pages). IRREVERSIBLE FILE OPERATION: the user is asked to confirm in a card first; on confirm every unsaved edit is saved to disk (cannot be undone) and the result is written as a NEW file in the default save folder and opened in a new tab; the current document keeps its pages.

function.name: split_pdf
function.description: Split the document into several PDF files of pages_per_file pages each (at least two files). A native folder picker opens for the user to choose where the files go; the current document keeps its pages. IRREVERSIBLE FILE OPERATION: the user is asked to confirm in a card first; on confirm every unsaved edit is saved to disk (cannot be undone) and the result is written as a NEW file in the default save folder and opened in a new tab; the current document keeps its pages.

pages_per_file.description: Pages per output file (1 to page count - 1)

function.name: transform_image
function.description: Move/resize an existing page image, or change its z-order relative to the text (takes effect on save). Call list_page_images first; image_number refers to that listing. Omitted parameters keep their current value; giving only width (or only height) scales the other side by the aspect ratio.

image_number.description: Image number from list_page_images (1-based, per page)

x.description: New left edge in points from the page left edge as displayed

y.description: New top edge in points from the page TOP edge as displayed

layer.description: Z-order relative to the page text

function.name: apply_ops
function.description:
Edit the document with a batch of ops — the same operations the editor's own toolbar performs. Ops run in order as one atomic batch: if any op fails, nothing is applied (the ops before it are undone) and the result names the failing op; otherwise the result lists what each op did.

[generated at runtime]

ops.description: Ordered list of op objects (see the op catalogue)

function.name: ask_clarification
function.description: Ask the user before an edit or an answer when the request is ambiguous about meaning, scope or target (which section or blocks, what a term, heading or table column in the document means, how far a rewrite should go). Shows a questionnaire card: 1–4 questions, ≤5 options each; the card adds "decide for me" and a free-text option itself. Use it only when a guess would likely change the wrong thing; skip it when the request or the document already answers it. Wait for the answers, then continue. Do not repeat the questions in your reply.

function.name: generate_image
function.description: Generate an illustration with AI from a text prompt and insert it into the document after a top-level block. For illustration/diagram-style art that image_search cannot find, or when the user asks to generate/draw a picture. The document must have been saved to disk at least once.

prompt.description: Image description in English, concrete and visual

afterIndex.description: 0-based block index to insert after; -1 = document start. Defaults to the end of the document.

function.name: get_document_context
function.description: Refresh the document overview: a numbered list of top-level blocks (index | type | preview) plus the current selection. Call this before index-based edits when in doubt.

function.name: image_search
function.description: Search for images. Returns a list of imageUrl entries; after picking one, insert it into the document with insert_image.

function.name: insert_image
function.description: Download a direct image link (an imageUrl from image_search) and insert it into the document after a top-level block. The image file is saved next to the document, so the document must have been saved to disk at least once.

afterIndex.description: 0-based block index to insert after; -1 = document start. Defaults to the end of the document.

function.name: read_blocks
function.description: Read a range of top-level blocks as markdown. Long output is paged; a notice tells you the offset to continue from.

offset.description: Character offset to continue a previously truncated read

function.name: read_frontmatter
function.description: Read the document properties: the raw YAML frontmatter block at the top of the file (title, tags, date, …), without the --- fences. Write it back with the setFrontmatter op.

function.name: web_search
function.description: Search the web for textual information (references/data/facts). Use when you need up-to-date information or are unsure about a fact. Returns titles/links/snippets.

function.name: write_document
function.description: [For long new content: a whole document, a chapter, a full report, article or translation] Hands the writing to the system writer, which streams markdown straight into the document while the user watches; you never write the text yourself. Give a concrete plan (title, section outline with the key points of each, tone, target length) and put every fact, figure, name and quote the text must use into context — the writer sees only the plan and context, not the conversation. Omit afterIndex on a blank document; on a document with content, pass afterIndex to insert after that block, or replaceDocument=true when the user asked to rewrite everything. Short additions (a paragraph or two) use apply_ops insertContent instead.

plan.description: title, section outline with key points per section, tone, target length

title.description: document/chapter title, when there is one

context.description: reference material: facts, figures, quotes, sources gathered from the conversation and web_search

afterIndex.description: insert after this block index (-1 = document start); omitted = whole document

replaceDocument.description: true replaces all existing content (only when the user asked for a rewrite)

function.name: apply_ops
function.description: Apply a batch of edits to the HTML source atomically: every op is validated first and either all are applied or none. Ops: `str_replace {old, new, sid?, replace_all?}` exact search-and-replace (old must match once; scope with sid when markup repeats); `replace_element {sid, html}` swap the whole element; `set_inner_html {sid, html}`; `set_text {sid, text}` (text is escaped for you); `insert_html {sid, position: before|after|prepend|append, html}`; `remove {sid}`; `move {sid, position: before|after, ref_sid}`; `set_attr {sid, name, value|null}`; `set_style {sid, styles: {prop: value|null}}` merges inline style. Prefer sid-addressed ops for single elements and str_replace for scattered text or CSS/JS edits. Keep unrelated markup, indentation and attribute order untouched. To place an attached image, write `attachment://` (the exact name from the attachment list) wherever a src/url value goes — set_attr value, an inside html, or a CSS url(); the app substitutes the real file itself. Never type base64 or data: URLs into ops, and never ask the user to paste base64.

summary.description: One short sentence shown to the user

function.name: ask_clarification
function.description: [Before creating a new page] Show a questionnaire card so the user makes the key choices (audience, scenario, tone, focus, length). Ask 2–4 questions that are real trade-offs for THIS topic, ≤5 options each; the card adds "decide for me" and a free-text option itself. Skip it when the request already answers these. Wait for the answers, then call plan_page. Do not repeat the questions in your reply.

function.name: get_outline
function.description: Structural outline of the document: one line per element with its line range, stable element id (sid), tag, id/class and a text preview. Use it to find where to read or edit. Narrow with from_sid / depth for large documents.

from_sid.description: Only this element and its subtree

function.name: plan_page
function.description: [Always before generating a new page or a full redesign, and when the user asks to restyle or "extract the brief" of an existing page] The system drafts the brief from this conversation (it reads the questionnaire answers, web_search findings, attachments and the page) and shows it to the user as style tiles with editable fields; pass only the mode and short notes. With mode "new" or "redesign" the confirmed brief is written into a page by the system right away (you do not write HTML yourself). Do not describe the brief in your reply.

mode.description: new = empty document, the page is generated after confirmation; redesign = the user asked to rebuild the whole page, generated after confirmation; restyle = keep the structure, you update --brief-* variables with apply_ops afterwards; extract = only pin the inferred brief

notes.description: At most three sentences the brief must honor: the choices the user made, a redo note, a direction hint. No facts or copy here; the writer reads the conversation.

function.name: read_attachment
function.description: Read the text content of an attachment (parsed locally). Long files are paged: read offset=0 first, then decide whether to continue based on the returned total character count.

index.description: attachment index (0-based, see the attachment list)

function.name: read_source
function.description: Read a slice of the HTML source with line numbers. Address by line range, or by sid to read one element. Long results are paged (page starts at 0).

function.name: web_search
function.description: Search the web for textual information (references/data/facts). Use when you need up-to-date information or are unsure about a fact. Returns titles/links/snippets.

function.name: write_document
function.description: [Content-first documents only: the user wants text written (article, guide, memo, announcement), not a designed page] Hands a plan to the system document writer, which writes the whole document as a clean single-column page. Give the title, a plan (outline, key points, length, voice) and the reference material in context. Everything else — new designed pages and full redesigns — goes through plan_page; single edits use apply_ops.

plan.description: outline and key points the document must cover, length, voice

context.description: facts, figures and source text the document must draw on

catalogue.name: generate_mindmap
catalogue.description: Render an interactive mind map of the document (or of one focused aspect) as a diagram card in the chat. Call it when the user asks for a mind map / 思维导图 / 脑图 / knowledge structure / overview diagram of the document or a topic. Pass the entire tree in this single call: the root is the document title or the focus topic, its children are the main sections, and so on. Labels must be short phrases in the document's own language and wording — never invent topics the document does not cover. Cite the block index each node summarizes in `block` so the user can jump to the passage. This tool does not modify the document; after it returns, reply with one short sentence.
